essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to determining where a text leaves matters uncertain change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what determining where a text leaves matters uncertain means on material that resists a first reading, and say where a competent reader would slow down.

Apply determining where a text leaves matters uncertain to 11-CCR material, working in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range, and distinguish what the text settles from what it leaves open.
State what the evidence does not establish, and what further evidence would settle it.
success_criteria: The response distinguishes what the text establishes from what it leaves uncertain.
Evidence is drawn from 11-CCR material and is quoted or located precisely enough to check.
The learner states what additional evidence would settle the open question.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on determining where a text leaves matters uncertain. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Ask the learner to attempt determining where a text leaves matters uncertain cold, before any instruction. Record what they already do well. Nothing here is scored, and errors here are data, not failure.
Name what the diagnostic revealed in neutral, non-character language. State the unit question and what will count as evidence by the end of it.

Walk the unit's destination: Produce an interpretive brief that argues from a text's deliberate uncertainties rather than around them.. The learner writes down what they think will be hardest about it and why. The tutor may question this prediction but may not write it.
The learner records one specific thing about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain they intend to be able to do by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Attempt determining where a text leaves matters uncertain without instruction, then record a personal goal for the unit.
formative_check: Name one thing about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain you can already do and one you cannot do yet.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for determining where a text leaves matters uncertain, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for determining where a text leaves matters uncertain works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about determining where a text leaves matters uncertain, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar 11-CCR text and state explicitly which conclusions the evidence does not support.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of determining where a text leaves matters uncertain in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Produce an interpretive brief that argues from a text's deliberate uncertainties rather than around them.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to where a story is set and how action is ordered change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?

Apply where a story is set and how action is ordered to 11-CCR material, working in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range, and distinguish what the text settles from what it leaves open.
State what the evidence does not establish, and what further evidence would settle it.
success_criteria: The response distinguishes what the text establishes from what it leaves uncertain.
Evidence is drawn from 11-CCR material and is quoted or located precisely enough to check.
The learner states what additional evidence would settle the open question.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on where a story is set and how action is ordered. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
Retrieve across the whole unit, not just today: the learner recalls the moves from earlier phases without notes first, then checks.

In one concise response, state the most important claim about where a story is set and how action is ordered and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: Interleaved practice across the unit's topics, deciding which move applies before applying it.

answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for where a story is set and how action is ordered, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for where a story is set and how action is ordered works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about where a story is set and how action is ordered, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of where a story is set and how action is ordered.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to addressing alternative or opposing perspectives change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what addressing alternative or opposing perspectives means on material that resists a first reading, and say where a competent reader would slow down.

Apply addressing alternative or opposing perspectives to 11-CCR material, working in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range, and distinguish what the text settles from what it leaves open.
State what the evidence does not establish, and what further evidence would settle it.
success_criteria: The response distinguishes what the text establishes from what it leaves uncertain.
Evidence is drawn from 11-CCR material and is quoted or located precisely enough to check.
The learner states what additional evidence would settle the open question.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: One last revision of the unit's product against the success criteria, focused on what is most significant for the audience.

Publish or present the work. This may be delivered publicly, privately to the facilitator, in writing, orally, or in another accessible format. No public or recorded performance is ever required, and media carries captions, transcripts, and alt text.
Place the piece beside earlier work and identify, with evidence, what changed about the learner's handling of addressing alternative or opposing perspectives and the unit's other topics.
Name what from this unit the next unit will assume you can already do.
File the piece with its target, evidence type, and revision history. Raw drafts and private reflections stay out of the guardian-visible record.

student_activity: Publish or present the unit's work in a chosen format, then evidence the growth it shows.
formative_check: Point to one concrete difference between this piece and your earlier work, and name what caused it.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for addressing alternative or opposing perspectives, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for addressing alternative or opposing perspectives works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about addressing alternative or opposing perspectives, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of addressing alternative or opposing perspectives.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar 11-CCR text and state explicitly which conclusions the evidence does not support.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting addressing alternative or opposing perspectives.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of addressing alternative or opposing perspectives in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Publish an argument portfolio and defend one sustained argument against substantive, prepared objections.
